instruction_summary: Re-estimate CDLZ (2019 QJE) minimum-wage bunching event study on data extended through 2024q4 events / 2025q4 outcomes, and show how the three headline claims (no job loss, wage gains, no break up to Kaitz ~0.59) evolved into the post-2016 $15-era.

steps.description: Read replication artifacts; confirmed baseline (Da=0.021, Db=-0.018, %dEmp=0.028, %dWage=0.068, OWE=0.411) from verdicts.json and replication_log.json; replication used pre-computed .dta so panel construction had to be rebuilt
Downloaded NBER MORG 2015-2024, Census Basic Monthly CPS 2025 (Oct missing=shutdown), VZ v1.4.0 MW zip
Built spliced CPI-U-RS (paper deflator) 1979-2016 + CPI-U growth 2017-2025, base 2016
Built state x quarter nominal MW panel 1979-2025 (VZ<=2016, VZ1.4.0 2017-2022, FRED STTMINWG + statutory mid-year schedule 2023-2025); sanity checks passed
Built CPS wage-bin count panel; VALIDATED by rebuilding 2016 from morg16.dta vs shipped panel (corr 1.00000, reldiff ~0); built 2017-2024 (MORG) + 2025 (Census)
Built event classification; VALIDATED belowshare corr 1.0 (maxdiff 8e-9), toosmall/fedincrease 100% agree, reproduced EXACTLY 138 prominent events for 1979-2016; 98 new events 2017-2024 (236 total)
Built I(tau,k) treatment/window/Omega-control dummies + calendar cohorts W1-W5 + ORIG; VALIDATED treat_p0/m1/p4 match shipped columns EXACTLY (100%), controls 98.5-99.9%
Pulled QCEW state total covered employment 1979-2025 via BLS open API; VALIDATED corr 1.00 vs shipped 2016 benchmark
Ran anchor (1979-2016), pooled 1979-2024, joint cohort W1-W5 regressions; ANCHOR reproduced paper (Da=0.021, Db=-0.018, E=0.571, bite=0.087)
C3 Kaitz split of W4+W5 events at 0.5 (events reach Kaitz 0.67, past paper's 0.59 frontier)
Produced flagship 3-panel figure and Figure II analog

key_results.kaitz_ge_0.5_pct_demp: -0.032 (se 0.043) -- negative but insignificant at bites up to 0.67
key_results.verdict: Findings HELD but SOFTENED: wage gains and bunching mechanism robust across eras; no window shows significant job loss, but central employment estimate drifted from +2.8% to ~0/slightly negative, concentrated in high-bite W4 and Kaitz>=0.5 events.

comparison_to_original.note: reproduced at anchor; softened to ~0/negative but never significantly negative in any window
held; smaller in recent windows as inflation eroded real bites

comparison_to_original.original: 138 events; no break up to Kaitz ~0.59
comparison_to_original.followup: 138 original (reproduced exactly) + 98 new; events reach Kaitz 0.67, %dEmp -3.2% (ns) at Kaitz>=0.5

deviations: Applied QCEW benchmarking (spec marked it optional/skip) via BLS QCEW open API, validated corr 1.00 vs shipped 2016; it materially affects normalization and the paper uses it.

2025 built from Census Basic Monthly CPS (MORG ends 2024); modest quarterly level seam vs 2024 MORG, absorbed by FEs and reported. Oct 2025 CPS/CPI missing (govt shutdown) -> 2025q4 from Nov+Dec only.
Event definition uses the paper's ground-truth do-file rule (real Delta MW > $0.25), which reproduces the 138 events exactly, rather than the spec's looser 'nominal >= $0.25' candidate wording.
Oregon MW uses the standard-rate statutory schedule because FRED STTMINWGOR reports the higher Portland-metro rate; NV two-tier seam smoothed via nominal non-decrease in 2017q1+.
Anchor %dEmp = 0.035 vs paper 0.028 (within 1 SE); Da, Db, E, bite, %dMW reproduce to 3 decimals. Traces to ~1.5% small-event-control discrepancy near the 2016 boundary.
Demographic/sector subgroups, placebo tail (k=+5..+17), and matched-CPS incumbent/entrant split were out of scope (three headline claims are overall estimates).
